clue.text: Two meeting a form of supreme council

indicators.note: a form of something is a version reshaped, so these letters are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Two people join a body that serves as the highest council in the land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form of' asks for a rearrangement of TWO, MEETING and A, eleven letters in all. The witenagemot was the council of Anglo-Saxon England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Anglo-Saxon kings were advised by this national assembly of nobles and churchmen, the top council of its day.

clue.text: The smallest possible present for Archbishop

parts.note: a whit is the least possible amount, as in 'not a whit'
a present is a gift

explanation.surface: Someone hunts for the tiniest gift that could be given to an archbishop.
explanation.walkthrough: John Whitgift was Archbishop of Canterbury under Elizabeth I.
explanation.definitionFit: John Whitgift held the see of Canterbury from 1583 to 1604, so the name identifies a senior churchman.

parts.note: a line of Thomas Gray's Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard with two words blanked out; the solver fills the gap from the poem

explanation.walkthrough: The full line in Gray's Elegy reads 'And shut the gates of mercy on mankind'; the dash marks the missing words.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing words of the quotation are the barriers of mercy that the ambitious man of the poem closes.

explanation.surface: A famous composition is the subject of a question.
explanation.walkthrough: A tune is set down in written form as a series of notes, so a piece of music is, punningly, something put into notes; the question mark flags that stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Famous people are called distinguished or celebrated; and music written down on the stave has been set in notation.

clue.text: Convert made us one of them

definitions.text: Convert made us one of them

parts.words: Convert made us one of them
parts.note: rearranging the letters of 'made us' gives the name of a snake-haired monster of Greek myth, and the answer is the group she belongs to

explanation.walkthrough: 'Convert made us' is an anagram, but its result is not entered: it names Medusa, and the answer is the trio she was one of.
explanation.definitionFit: Medusa and her two sisters were the snake-haired monsters of Greek myth whose gaze turned onlookers to stone.

clue.text: With German support, fellow you hear set #ce

indicators.note: in a down clue a support goes underneath, so the German word comes last

parts.note: a fellow is a man

indicators.note: 'you hear' says the word you is wanted as it sounds, the single letter

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like U
mit is the German word for with

explanation.surface: A man, backed by Germans, is told to release someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Support' puts the German word for 'with' at the foot of this down entry, under MAN and U. The definition is printed 'set #ce', a misprint of 'set free'.
explanation.definitionFit: To manumit is the formal term for releasing a slave from bondage.

indicators.note: what the letters could be when rearranged signals an anagram

explanation.surface: A remark that a clothes dryer might turn out to be poor quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could be' tells you to rearrange the nine letters of DRIER and THAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of poor quality is described as third-rate, a step below second-best.

explanation.surface: Someone arranges a con.
explanation.definitionFit: To fix an outcome dishonestly, as a match or election, is to rig it; and a rig is also a swindle or dodge.

clue.text: Recruit — man on board that is

parts.note: a rook is a chess piece, a man on the chessboard
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A new recruit is described as the man on the board, that is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man on board' looks like a sailor or a director, but it is a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A recruit is a newcomer, and a beginner in any field is called a rookie.

parts.note: 24 across is a formal party or welcome function, and the people invited go to it

explanation.definitionFit: Invited visitors at a wedding party or other function are the people who come to it.

indicators.note: the second half of the word tells you to alter the order of the letters in its first half

explanation.surface: A passive form of road junction.
explanation.walkthrough: The single word 'interchange' splits into 'inter', the fodder, and 'change', the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inactive and unresponsive, doing nothing, is described as inert.

clue.text: Scold one European for being reckless type

parts.note: to scold is to rant at someone
I is the Roman numeral for one
a Pole is a European from Poland

explanation.surface: One European scolds another for being reckless.
explanation.walkthrough: Rantipole is an old word for a wild, rakish person.
explanation.definitionFit: A rantipole is a wild, unruly romp of a person, someone heedless and rash.

parts.note: to watch over something is to guard it
space is room

explanation.surface: A lookout post by the doors of a railway station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Station' is a military station, not a railway one: the guard's quarters are by the camp gate.
explanation.definitionFit: On a military base the room for the soldiers on guard duty is placed at the main gate.

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a crossword shorthand for many
a rift is a split or disagreement

explanation.surface: Someone drove a crowd to quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drove' is a noun here, a herd of cattle on the move, not the past of drive.
explanation.definitionFit: A drove is a herd being driven along, and a drift is likewise a herd or flock moving together.

indicators.note: one word is placed around the other, outside it

parts.note: one who flees runs off and disappears
EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: A thief robs people and then vanishes beyond the City limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' with a capital means the City of London, the financial district, whose postcode letters are the usual crossword stand-in.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleece someone is to swindle them out of their money.

clue.text: Accusation precludes your being one of twelve

definitions.text: precludes your being one of twelve

explanation.surface: Being accused bars you from jury service.
explanation.walkthrough: In court a lawyer can object to a juror; that objection stops the person from being one of the twelve on the jury.
explanation.definitionFit: An old sense of the word is a charge or claim against someone; and an objection to a juror removes them from the panel of twelve.

clue.text: Speak Afrikaans thanks to a student

parts.note: ta is informal British for thank you
L, the learner plate, stands for a student

explanation.surface: Thanking a student in Afrikaans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speak' is a noun here, as in 'tech-speak': the language itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The Taal was the old name for the Dutch-derived language of South Africa, now known as Afrikaans.

indicators.note: a new version of these words is a rearrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: Someone mentions a fresh name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' tells you to rearrange MENTION and A.
explanation.definitionFit: To name someone for a post or award is to put them forward as a candidate.

clue.text: Boy has doubt — not born to hold the stage

parts.note: Stan is a boy's name

indicators.note: the word tells you to drop the letter for born from the other word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A lad unsure of himself, not a natural performer, takes the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not born' removes B from DOUBT, leaving DOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To be conspicuous and draw all eyes is to command attention, as an actor holding the stage does.

parts.note: the phrase calls to mind the idiom for a spouse, better plus one word, and the answer is that missing word

explanation.definitionFit: A man's wife is jocularly called his better half, the superior partner.

parts.note: a form is a long bench without a back
a worker ant, a crossword staple

explanation.surface: Someone describes a decisive person working on a bench.
explanation.walkthrough: A form is an old British school bench. In linguistics a formant is a part of a word that determines its type.
explanation.definitionFit: A formant is a forming element of a word, such as an affix, which settles its grammatical class.

clue.text: Beer the price of a herb

parts.note: ale is a beer
price is cost

explanation.surface: Someone compares a beer with what a herb costs.
explanation.walkthrough: Alecost, also called costmary, was once used to flavour ale.
explanation.definitionFit: Alecost is costmary, an aromatic plant once used to flavour ale.

explanation.surface: An elderly flag-carrier.
explanation.walkthrough: Ancient is an old form of ensign, a flag or its bearer: Iago in Othello is called the Moor's ancient.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of great age is described as antique; and an ensign, the soldier carrying the colours, was once called an ancient.

parts.note: Long is a proper name here, the New York landmark, of which this is the kind of place

explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like a verb meaning yearn, or an adjective; it is Long Island, off New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Long Island is a piece of land surrounded by water off the coast of New York.

clue.text: Pour cold water over mother swan

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother
a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: Someone discourages a mother swan.
explanation.walkthrough: A dam is a mother animal, and a pen is a female swan (the male is a cob).
explanation.definitionFit: To pour cold water over a plan is to discourage it, to make it less lively.

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
complete means all, the whole

explanation.surface: A way of bringing something to a full halt.
explanation.definitionFit: To stall is to come to a halt, as an engine does, or to delay.

parts.note: a frosty greeting from one's hosts is the opposite of a warm welcome

explanation.definitionFit: A cold greeting is unfriendly, so a frosty manner of being received is unwelcoming.

clue.text: Father takes in wood for old Turkish governor.

indicators.note: one word takes the other inside it

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
ash is a wood

explanation.surface: A father collects wood for an Ottoman official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wood' here is a timber tree, not a forest; 'takes in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pasha was a high-ranking provincial governor or officer in the Ottoman Empire.

clue.text: A very soft finish takes time.. if something added

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very soft
a finish is an end
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A quiet ending takes a while if something extra is attached.
explanation.walkthrough: PP is pianissimo, the musical sign for very quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: An appendage is an attachment, something joined on to a larger thing.

clue.text: Maybe ask how Manx get head-dress

indicators.note: maybe says the letters might be arranged differently
a Manx cat has no tail, so the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone wonders how the people of the Isle of Man come by their hats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manx' cuts the tail off HOW to give HO; 'Maybe' then rearranges ASK with HO.
explanation.definitionFit: A shako is a tall military cap with a peak and a plume.

indicators.note: only half of the word is kept, its first three letters going

parts.note: London is the capital of the UK

explanation.surface: Half of London is splendid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swell' is a noun, a fine gentleman, not a verb or adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A swell is a toff or dignitary, and a don is a Spanish gentleman or a distinguished academic.

clue.text: He may bring about a good move

definitions.text: He may bring about a good move

parts.words: He may bring about a good move
parts.note: the move is a change of house, which a property agent arranges, not a move in chess or a game

explanation.definitionFit: The professional who sells houses helps buyers relocate to a new home.
